data.holdout: THIS SWEEP IS THE HOLDOUT. The window was sealed when SW-0032 was frozen and has not been loaded, plotted or summarised. It can be spent exactly once: any rerun, parameter change or second look makes it in-sample forever. The universe file for this window must be built fresh at run time, using only data available then.
symbols: point-in-time top 20 by prior-month quote volume

decision_rule.note: CONFIRMED if z >= +2. REFUTED if z <= -2. INCONCLUSIVE otherwise, which on the power analysis below is the MOST LIKELY OUTCOME and is recorded as inconclusive rather than retried on a longer window. Fixed before any result was computed. Not adjustable.

derived.note: Detection limit for the population test: the smallest TRUE mean market-neutral gross Sharpe, across the whole search space, that this design could distinguish from shuffled data with 80% power. Says nothing about any individual variant.

hypothesis: SW-0032 and SW-0034 were the only sweeps in this registry to approach the threshold: DSR 0.809 and 0.823 against a 0.95 bar, best annualised Sharpe 0.98 and 0.99 against an expected-under-null of 0.64 and 0.62, with 96% of variants positive. A post-hoc split showed the effect comes entirely from long-lived symbols (net Sharpe 0.72 for the 81 symbols with more than 40,000 bars, against 0.04 for the 55 with fewer than 20,000), which is the opposite of what a spurious altcoin-volatility artefact would look like. Prediction: on data never inspected, the same enumerated space will again produce a positive mean net Sharpe across variants.

planning.power_note: STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE RESULT: this test is underpowered and will probably not resolve anything. The standard error of an annualised Sharpe over n bars is sqrt(8760/n), so confirming a true Sharpe of 0.72 at z=2 with 80% power needs about 136,000 hourly bars — roughly 15.6 years, i.e. 2041. Four years gives around 29% power. Testing the per-asset information coefficient instead does not rescue it: the implied IC is about 0.008, and asset-periods are not independent because assets move together, so the effective sample is far smaller than the raw count. Four years was chosen as the longest window that is still actionable rather than the shortest that might look decisive. An effect of this size may simply not be confirmable by a solo researcher on public data, and if so that is itself worth recording.
planning.sd_source: Null sd scaled from the SW-0002 measurement of 0.062 over 68,490 observations to roughly 35,000 observations, then widened because a cross-sectional portfolio has fewer effectively independent bets than a single-asset sweep. Estimated before the data was touched; the diagnostic measures the true null directly and the record reports both.

protocol.execution_model: weights set from bar t close, held over bar t+1, cost charged on the size of every weight change
protocol.method: Identical to SW-0032. Equal-weighted, dollar-neutral unless exit_rule is long-only.
protocol.survivorship_note: universe rebuilt monthly from prior-month volume; delisted symbols retained for the months they traded

search_space.enumeration_note: Identical to SW-0032. Not one parameter changed. Altering the space between the discovery sample and the holdout would destroy the only thing this test provides.

title: Holdout test: cross-sectional momentum across a point-in-time top-20 crypto universe
